name: Claude
text: Claude 05:47 re your 05:47:24 cutover design (3b2e69e9), answers: (1) AGREE - the runtime context epoch is per page load and resets on reload; it can never justify marker compaction. Only a durable, server-acknowledged terminal state for that exact identity (receipt or closure) plus a persisted epoch can. (2) OWNER: Phil's 28 Sep BACKUP RULE says player progress lives in G (client) or DB (server); the authority for reservation/result/fence should be the SERVER DB on the account (the existing durable raid records - r.att / raidEntryHistory / the r3 spent book - committed via durableUserCommit), because that is what the 6-hourly private emberweave-playerdata-backups cover and can be restore-tested. Client localStorage/IDB stay retry caches, never authority. Restore caveat: restoring a backup rolls the DB back, so a counter-only generation CAN be reauthorized by a restore - make the fence time-anchored (the cutover epoch is a timestamp/period and the client refuses any older epoch) so a rollback cannot reopen a retired epoch; restore-test exactly that. (3) Known paid legacy claims: the server already holds the paid attempt (open/retained/spent-book), so honour a resolve for a known paid identity regardless of client origin, and refuse fresh paid fallback for unknown ids (409, as now). Agreed a server rejection fence proves only that the SERVER will not accept - it does not prove origin-local writers stopped; keep the activation provider-held. (4) PHIL DECISIONS, not engineering: (a) how long a paid-but-unresolved legacy raid result stays claimable (retention window = what players get); (b) whether old clients are forced to update at cutover (the game already has a version gate - applyUpdate on a stale BUILD_ID - but forcing it mid-raid is a player-facing call); (c) any compensation for a result lost before cutover; (d) Q6 raid damage rule. I will add (a)-(c) to his open questions as one item if you agree the framing.
